metadata.scope: e_deccan (166 non-867 baronies across k_andhra, k_karnata, k_lanka, k_maharastra, k_tamilakam, and k_telingana; excludes baronies where is_historical_at['867'] is true)
metadata.hierarchy_note: hierarchy reflects data/ck3_title_tree.json (save-derived de jure tree including x_script_* dynamic titles); downstream localisation/historicity mods should key on barony_key and join against their target landed_titles tree.

schema_notes.vanilla_ck3_name: Exact English localisation string from CK3 titles_l_english.yml.
schema_notes.modern_name: Clean modern/standard English display name of the audited settlement or holding.
schema_notes.modern_name_note: Optional administrative parent, alternate designation, or native-script qualifier; null if none.
schema_notes.hierarchy: De jure title hierarchy from data/ck3_title_tree.json (empire, kingdom, duchy, county, holding_type).
schema_notes.is_historical_at: Bookmark-keyed booleans {'867', '1066', '1178'}; all entries here have '867': false.
schema_notes.replacement_candidates: List of exactly 3 associated natural feature names and historical tribal/ethnonym names (>=1 tribe per barony) usable as localisation replacements.
schema_notes.name: Clean display name of the replacement candidate (Wikipedia disambiguation suffixes extracted to disambiguation_note).
schema_notes.disambiguation_note: Optional disambiguator extracted from parenthetical/comma qualifiers (e.g. 'Liao', 'Orkney', 'river'); null if none.
schema_notes.localisation_stem: Clean CK3-ready toponym stem stripped of redundant generic English feature suffixes/prefixes ('River', 'Mount', 'Lake', 'people', etc.) while preserving meaningful compounds.
schema_notes.attestation_basis: Historicity classification distinguishing genuinely pre-867/pre-literate entities from medieval post-867 ethnogeneses: attested_pre_867 | indigenous_pre_literate | attested_867_to_1066 | attested_1066_to_1178.
schema_notes.valid_for_bookmarks: Bookmark-keyed booleans {'867', '1066', '1178'} indicating whether the replacement candidate is historically non-anachronistic for that bookmark (true for both attested_pre_867 and indigenous_pre_literate; bookmark-gated for attested_867_to_1066 and attested_1066_to_1178).
schema_notes.candidates_with_multilingual_variants: Count of replacement candidates having more than 1 distinct language_code (ISO 639-3 / ISO 639-5 or documented proto-stage code) across language_variants.
schema_notes.language_variants_policy: Include core local/classical forms plus regionally scoped vernaculars and genuinely distinct exonyms; exclude out-of-region exonym padding and redundant eng copies (eng is retained only when no non-English variant exists). Uses ISO 639-3 / ISO 639-5 language_code values plus documented Wiktionary proto/stage codes (sla-pro, gem-pro, cel-pro, cel-bry, urj-fin-pro); reconstructed proto/ancient forms carry a leading '*'.
schema_notes.language_variants: List of cultural/historical name forms: {form, native_script, language, language_code, notes}. form is always clean Latin script (or romanization) suitable for CK3 localisation; native_script holds the native non-Latin script form or null when the language natively uses Latin script.
schema_notes.relationship: Prose description of the geographical, ecological, or historical relationship between the replacement entity and the audited barony.
schema_notes.etymology_notes: Linguistic etymology, onomastic origin, or geographic/ethnographic characterization of the replacement entity (incorporating attested onomastic notes from language variants where documented).
